text: Sir Timothy Shelley, 2nd Baronet (7 September 1753 – 24 April 1844), was an English politician and lawyer. He was the son of Sir Bysshe Shelley, 1st Baronet, and Mary Catherine Michell (1734–1760), daughter of the Reverend Theobald Michell and Mary Tredcroft. Timothy studied at University College, Oxford, earning his bachelor's degree in 1778 and his master's degree in 1781, before studying law at Lincoln's Inn. He was elected as a member of parliament (MP) for Horsham, Sussex, in the 1790 general election, but the result was overturned on 19 March 1792 due to an election petition. He was elected as MP for New Shoreham at the 1802 general election and was re-elected for Shoreham in 1806, 1807, and 1812, holding the seat until he stood down at the 1818 general election. During his political career, he associated with the Duke of Norfolk. Timothy married Elizabeth Pilfold in October 1791 and moved to Field Place in Warnham, West Sussex, about 40 miles (64 km) outside London. The couple had seven children, none of whom married except Mary, who married D. F. Haynes in 1819. He inherited the baronetcy on 6 January 1815, becoming the 2nd Baronet Shelley of Castle Goring, Sussex. He was also the father of Romantic poet and dramatist Percy Bysshe Shelley.
